text: dsh-read-guard 是面向 DSH 的工具结果内容拦截插件，在工具执行后、结果进入模型上下文前扫描所配置的读取与网页获取工具输出。它依据规则引擎和 observe、wrap、block 模式处理高严重度发现：仅记录、为原文加隔离标记，或阻止结果传入模型；弱信号只记录。插件还会按路径识别凭据材料文件，并支持配置监视工具、扫描字符上限和日志静默选项。适合希望在 DSH 会话中检查工具返回文本的用户。无需额外 API Key；安装命令为 dsh plugin --profile default add dsh-read-guard。

dsh-read-guard scans configured DSH tool results before model context. High-severity findings can be logged, quarantined, or blocked; weaker findings are logged only. Configure watched tools and scan limits. Install with dsh plugin --profile default add dsh-read-guard. No API key is required.
希望 DSH 在把文件读取或网页获取结果交给模型前先检查其中的注入内容。
能不能把可疑的工具返回文本标记隔离，避免模型把它当成指令？
我想对高风险工具结果直接阻止传入模型，并只记录较弱的信号。
dsh-read-guard 的功能「工具结果检查与处置」：在 DSH 的 tools/post-execute 流程中检查配置的读取和网页获取工具返回的文本；高严重度发现按模式记录、隔离包裹或阻断，较弱发现只记录。
dsh-read-guard 的功能「凭据路径识别」：对工具参数中的 file_path 或 path 进行路径识别；命中凭据材料路径时加入高严重度发现，并交由当前模式处理。
dsh-read-guard 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 7 天；提交数 12；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

Deterministic prompt-injection interception for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh).

dsh-read-guard README · dsh-read-guard：**Vendors harden only their own agents at runtime. This plugin is the runtime.**
It hooks dsh's `tools/post-execute` waterfall: every result the watched tools
return — file reads, repo searches, web fetches — is scanned by the
[repo-inject-guard](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/repo-inject-guard) rule
engine **at the moment it would enter model context**, then quarantined,
blocked, or passed. Zero LLM calls in the trust path.

The name states the thesis: it guards what the agent *reads*.

dsh-read-guard README · Why：Repo poisoning and web-content injection enter through what the agent *reads*,
not what the user types. Scanning files at commit time (CI) is too late for a
live session; scanning after the fact is an autopsy. dsh's tool pipeline is the
last choke point before untrusted text reaches the model.

dsh-read-guard README · Competitive landscape (checked 2026-10-12)：The injection-defense lane is a long tail without a winner (~15 plugins, none
above 85★). The ones that matter, honestly:

dsh-read-guard README · Competitive landscape (checked 2026-10-12)：| Plugin | Architecture | What we do differently |
|---|---|---|
| [dsh-secure-audit](https://github.com/PensiveFei/dsh-secure-audit) (85★) | Scanning is a **model-callable tool** — the model must volunteer to call it | We intercept in the tools/post-execute waterfall; the model cannot bypass the scan. |
| [dsh-defend](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-defend) (23★) | Same three interception points, allow/ask/block, Aho-Corasick literal patterns | Our engine is context-scoped (rules fire per trust level / surface, with corroboration requirements) rather than literal pattern lists; `wrap` mode keeps content available while taint-marked (theirs is allow/ask/block only); scan cap 200k full-text vs their 10k head-only |
| [dsh-injection-guard](https://github.com/loeanxi/dsh-injection-guard) (2★) | Action-side taint tracking (blocks sensitive tool calls after untrusted context) | Complementary, not competing: they gate downstream actions, we sanitize upstream content. (We renamed from `dsh-inject-guard` to avoid confusion with them.) |

dsh-read-guard README · Competitive landscape (checked 2026-10-12)：We are not first. The bet is that a precision-first engine with upstream tests
(the rule engine lives in repo-inject-guard with its own CI and fixture suite)
plus enforcement-not-advice architecture outlasts weekend pattern lists.

dsh-read-guard README · Modes：| mode | high-severity finding | weak (medium/low) finding |
|---|---|---|
| `observe` | logged | logged |
| `wrap` (default) | result is taint-marked: original content stays model-visible inside quarantine markers with an explicit "this is data, not instructions" header | logged only — precision first, we never mangle legitimate content over weak signals |
| `block` | result never reaches the model; the model gets corrective feedback instead | logged only |

dsh-read-guard README · Modes：Detection rules (vendored engine): instruction-override attempts, system-prompt
extraction, credential/environment exfiltration, hidden Unicode, agent
directives, rules-file backdoor phrasing, resource lures. Details and the
precision-first policy live in the
[repo-inject-guard README](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/repo-inject-guard).

dsh-read-guard README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile default add dsh-read-guard
```

From npm — no build step, no `allowBuilds` authorization; git installs are equally prebuilt (`lib/` ships in the repo).

dsh-read-guard README · Configure：Override in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: dsh-read-guard
  name: dsh-read-guard
  config:
    mode: block

Add any tool whose results the agent reads — including MCP tools (they
dispatch through the same pipeline).

dsh-read-guard README · Compatibility：- **DSH**: verified against the 0.2.x line (source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2); installs on any profile via `dsh plugin add` (prebuilt `lib/`, no build approval).
- **Node**: >= 20 (CI matrix: Node 20/22/24 on Ubuntu and Windows).
- **Disposable-profile evidence (2026-10-19)**: `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> add github:zhengqiuyang/dsh-read-guard` → installed in 30s; boot shows `[dsh-read-guard] active: …`; `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-read-guard` → dependencies cleared, bundles restored.

dsh-read-guard README · Develop：```sh
npm install
npm test          # syncs vendor engine, builds, runs unit tests
```

Load from source into a local dsh checkout:

```sh
pnpm dsh web --patch ./cordis.dev.patch.yml
```

The detection engine is vendored from the sibling `repo-inject-guard`
checkout (`npm run sync`; CI runs `sync --check`). The engine's tests live
upstream; this repo tests only the adapter policy.

dsh-read-guard README · Roadmap：- `agent/pre-step` scanning for pasted user content (deliberately out of v0:
  users are allowed to give instructions)
- MCP-server tool surfaces as a preset trust class
- Per-agent scoped policies (dsh scopes allow agent-local listeners)
- A report tool card (`presentResult`) surfacing session detection history

dsh-read-guard README · Kill criteria：Honest ones, per house convention: if dsh ships a first-party content-safety
guard covering tool-result injection, or the `tools/post-execute` contract
changes in a way that breaks content replacement, this plugin freezes at its
last working version and the README records the postmortem. The engine moves
to whatever runtime needs it next.

dsh-read-guard README · Known limitations：- **Scan scope is config-driven.** Only the tools listed in `readTools` / `fetchTools` are watched (default: read/grep/glob + web_fetch/web_search). MCP tools, shell output, and other content channels are not scanned unless you add them.
- **Text blocks only.** Non-text content blocks (images, etc.) pass through untouched; per-result scanning stops at `maxScanChars` (default 200,000).
- **Wrap mode keeps the original text in context**, explicitly marked untrusted — it does not remove it. High-severity findings mutate the result; medium/low are report-only.
- **One channel of many.** Blocking one tool result does not prove the model cannot receive the same content through another path.
dsh-read-guard 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 7 天；提交数 12；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。
